name: Ilford Delta 100 Professional
notes: Read from the Maco Direct mirror of the older '100 DELTA PROFESSIONAL' edition (ilford-delta-100-maco.pdf, 6 pages, no date, no document code): its spectral curve is a vector path (exact) and the characteristic plot is as clear as in the official Apr 2023 sheet (ilford-delta-100.pdf, 7 pages), which carries the same ID-11 / 8.5 min curve and the same spectrogram as scanned images; the two curves agree by eye (about density 1.0 at relative log exposure 3). The official sheet (footer 'Apr 2023') would give date 2023-04.

Characteristic curve: x axis is RELATIVE log exposure (frame 0 to 4.5, no absolute lux-seconds, no Log H Ref), y is density, frame bottom = 0 (gridlines every 0.5, labelled 1.0 and 2.0). Densitometry type is not stated; balance 'daylight' is the light of the ISO 100/21 speed rating ('to daylight').

One curve only: roll film in ILFORD ID-11 stock, 8.5 min at 20C, intermittent agitation, said to represent 35mm and sheet film too. Traced as v; base+fog about 0.08 as read, curve ends at relative log exposure about 4.05 (density about 1.8, still rising, no shoulder). Where the curve crosses a horizontal gridline the traced value can be off by up to about 0.02 density (grid removal splits the ink).

Spectral sensitivity: 'Wedge spectrogram to tungsten light (2850K)' drawn as a vector line curve on a 'Sensitivity' axis with ticks 0.5 and 1.0 only; traced as sensitivity/v with numbers as printed (relative; linear or log not stated). The frame bottom is about 0.05 on that scale; the curve runs about 356-657 nm.
